title: Risk-stratified osteoporosis assessment and management
purpose: Clinician-reviewed decision support; not a validated autonomous prescribing engine.
scope: Postmenopausal women and men aged 50 years or older; adapt to local guidelines and prescribing rules.

user_supplied_modifications: FRAX with femoral neck BMD when available; TBS may refine estimates.
Hip or spine fragility fracture indicates at least high risk regardless of BMD.
Add unknown/unassessed and moderate categories, numeric FRAX thresholds, and risk-tier reassessment guidance.
provenance.interpretation_note: Where the source image and user-supplied criteria differ, this JSON applies the user-supplied criteria.

required_before_category: History of fragility fractures, including site, number, and date
DXA BMD and T-scores at lumbar spine, total hip, and femoral neck when available
FRAX 10-year hip and major osteoporotic fracture (MOF) probabilities
Review of secondary causes, medications, falls, frailty, and treatment history
imaging_and_tests_when_indicated: Vertebral fracture assessment or spinal imaging when clinically indicated
Evaluate secondary causes and investigate unexplained or discordant findings

frax.without_bmd: FRAX may be calculated without BMD when DXA is unavailable, but complete DXA assessment when appropriate.
frax.tbs: Trabecular bone score may refine fracture-risk estimates when available.

thresholds.local_thresholds: Apply applicable national intervention thresholds; where they differ from these stated thresholds, document the guideline used.

frax.interpretation: Many fractures occur in people whose T-score is above -2.5; consider clinical risk factors alongside BMD.

universal_foundation.applies_to: All patients, including those awaiting assessment and those receiving medication
measures: Calcium intake 1000-1200 mg/day, preferably from diet; supplement only the dietary shortfall as appropriate
Vitamin D 600-800 IU/day, individualized to clinical context and measured status where indicated
Adequate nutrition and review of bone-harmful medicines

decision_sequence: Check whether the patient is within the population scope.
If no DXA or fracture-risk estimate has been completed, classify as unknown/unassessed and complete assessment before choosing pharmacotherapy.
If none apply, evaluate high-risk criteria.
If neither high nor very high apply, distinguish low from moderate risk using BMD and fracture probability.
If information is missing, unreliable, or unresolved, classify as indeterminate and complete or refer for assessment.

unknown_unassessed.label: Unknown (not yet assessed)
criteria: No DXA or fracture-risk estimate yet.
action: Obtain DXA BMD, assess for vertebral fracture when indicated, and calculate FRAX.
unknown_unassessed.medication: Do not select osteoporosis pharmacotherapy solely from an unassessed result; known high-risk evidence should be preserved while evaluation is completed.

very_high.label: Very high
criteria: T-score < -3.0 at a valid site
Recent fragility fracture within the past 12 months
Multiple fragility fractures
Fracture while receiving osteoporosis therapy
Fracture with a bone-harmful medication exposure, such as long-term glucocorticoids
High fall risk
FRAX 10-year hip fracture probability > 4.5% OR MOF probability > 30%
action: Consider referral to an osteoporosis specialist, especially with vertebral fractures, complex secondary causes, or advanced CKD.
Consider anabolic-first therapy, followed sequentially by an antiresorptive to maintain gains.
If anabolic therapy is unsuitable, select an appropriate potent antiresorptive with specialist or clinician review.
very_high.sequencing: After completing anabolic therapy, start an antiresorptive without an avoidable gap, subject to the selected drug's prescribing guidance.
very_high.rationale: For very-high-risk patients, anabolic-first treatment can provide greater vertebral-fracture reduction than antiresorptive-first treatment.

high.label: High
criteria: T-score <= -2.5 at lumbar spine, total hip, or femoral neck
Prior hip or vertebral fragility fracture, regardless of BMD
FRAX 10-year hip fracture probability >= 3% OR MOF probability >= 20%
Another clinician-confirmed treatment indication from a secondary-condition pathway
action: Offer pharmacological treatment after checking contraindications, renal function, and patient-specific factors.
Usually choose an oral or IV bisphosphonate as first-line treatment.
Denosumab is an option when bisphosphonates are contraindicated or not tolerated; plan ongoing treatment and an exit/transition strategy before starting.
Raloxifene may be considered for an appropriate woman without thromboembolic risk who declines bisphosphonates.
high.renal_note: Bisphosphonate eligibility depends on the specific drug and renal function. If eGFR is below approximately 30-35 mL/min/1.73 m2, bisphosphonates may be unsuitable; evaluate for CKD-MBD and seek renal-bone expertise before choosing an alternative.

moderate.label: Moderate
criteria: T-score between -1.0 and -2.5, with values at -2.5 or below assigned to high risk
FRAX hip probability < 3% AND MOF probability < 20%
No very-high-risk or high-risk criterion
action: Individualize the decision to use pharmacotherapy based on clinical risk factors, patient preferences, and applicable national guidance.
options_when_treatment_is_chosen: Menopausal hormone therapy in an appropriate candidate

low.label: Low
criteria: T-score > -1.0, or osteopenia with low fracture probability
FRAX hip probability < 3% AND MOF probability < 20%
No high-risk or very-high-risk feature
Fracture and secondary-cause review is complete, and DXA is reliable or an accepted assessment supports low risk
action: No osteoporosis pharmacotherapy based on this result alone.
Continue universal lifestyle measures and reassess periodically or earlier if clinical circumstances change.
low.reassessment: Typically every 2-4 years; reassess sooner with a new fracture, new risk factor, significant medication change, or other clinical change.

indeterminate.label: Indeterminate
criteria: Important information is missing or unresolved, including age, menopause status, fracture history, or decisive testing
DXA is unreliable or discordant
A secondary condition or another fragility fracture needs assessment
The patient is outside the population scope
action: Complete the missing assessment, refer, or use the relevant specialist pathway.
Do not default to low risk.
If high-risk evidence is already known, retain at least the high-risk designation while clarifying.

priority_rules: Classify as very high if any very-high-risk criterion is present, even if BMD has improved during treatment.
A prior hip or vertebral fragility fracture alone establishes at least high risk regardless of BMD.
A low T-score does not override a higher fracture-risk category.
If multiple categories could apply, use the highest supported category.
Do not label a patient low risk until fracture history, secondary causes, and relevant assessment are sufficiently complete.

secondary_conditions.principle: Secondary conditions modify assessment and treatment selection; they do not automatically imply the same risk tier for every patient.
secondary_conditions.action: Review the condition-specific pathway, medications, and fracture risk. A clinician-confirmed treatment indication may support high risk; recent or multiple fractures or fracture on therapy may support very high risk.

ckd_and_current_therapy.advanced_ckd_or_suspected_ckd_mbd: Obtain renal-bone specialist input for treatment selection and preserve any already established risk tier.
ckd_and_current_therapy.no_dxa: Absence of DXA does not mean low risk; complete risk assessment.
ckd_and_current_therapy.improved_bmd_on_treatment: Improved BMD does not erase the prior osteoporosis diagnosis or fracture history.
ckd_and_current_therapy.denosumab: Do not stop or delay denosumab without a clinician-led plan for ongoing therapy or antiresorptive transition.

follow_up.low_risk: Reassess fracture risk typically every 2-4 years, or sooner for clinical change.
follow_up.moderate_risk: Individualize reassessment interval based on baseline risk, treatment choice, and clinical change.
follow_up.high_or_very_high_on_therapy: Reassess more frequently than low-risk patients; interval depends on drug, adherence, fracture status, BMD response, and clinical risk.
drug_specific_review: Review duration and continuation of bisphosphonate therapy and whether a monitored drug holiday is appropriate.
Do not use a drug holiday with denosumab; plan sequential antiresorptive therapy if it is discontinued.
After anabolic treatment, use sequential antiresorptive therapy to maintain gains.

implementation_notes: These criteria are a clinical decision-support framework and should be applied with local guidelines, drug labels, contraindications, and clinician judgment.
FRAX thresholds and treatment availability can vary by country; record which national threshold was applied.
T-score thresholds apply to valid DXA measurements at accepted skeletal sites.
Treatment choice should account for renal function, pregnancy potential where relevant, thromboembolic risk, cardiovascular risk when considering romosozumab, patient preferences, and access.
